inspectionPaging: pickups and scene_nodes reserve escaped row size before projection and may shorten pages; nextOffset continues complete identities. A row that cannot fit returns too_large. Pickup queries have a cumulative 32 MiB copy allowance; omit query and page if exceeded. preview_state accepts offset (default 0) and limit (1..200, default 100) for texturePacks only, with texturePackCount, texturePackOffset and texturePackNextOffset; complete Name/Path choices remain shared with the GUI and scene_options.
discovery: Document source-workspace summaries retain counts and undo/redo status without duplicating dirty-file/history arrays across open missions; source_changes returns those shared bounded details. dirtyFilesTruncated/historyTruncated disclose omitted rows. Initialize, tools/list, resources/list and capabilities inspection are windowless. The first valid workspace request attaches or launches the opted-in GUI. Embedded command metadata is generated from the live registry and parity-tested. Camera position/look arrays have exactly three numeric elements; rotate/zoom screenPoint has exactly two viewport DIP coordinates; export array items require kind/index identities. Terrain path coordinates are numeric [x,z] pairs within ±1,000,000; polygons require an outer ring and optional same-shaped hole rings, each with 3–200,000 points. Recursive item validation rejects invalid_argument before handlers or workspace connection. Pickup source identities have four required typed fields; destination maps have string values; integers advertise handler-compatible bounds.
inspection: Folder indexing retains at most 250,000 asset rows and 8,388,608 name characters. open_root, search and related expose indexComplete and indexNotice; totals describe indexed matches. The GUI discloses incomplete indexing and Files/direct opening remain available. Related asset lookup uses one bounded index scan, preserves case-insensitive filename-stem/reference-order matching, and reports truncated when indexing is incomplete or reference, index or result limits are reached; the GUI Related tab shows the same limitation. World comparison retains primary-root names and material texture directory-occurrence identities. Source builds retain XZ horizon bindings and report unsupported camera mutations. Automatic texture planning rereads current PNG headers. World comparison uses node counterparts for area, camera, light and sound references, preserving area multiplicity; duplicate-name reference details include slots. Import refuses unrepresentable engine names and malformed engine metadata/material vectors; reconstruction rejects differing duplicate scripts and bounds image-resource strings before normalization. Source checks and exports refuse known animation engine-load failures independently of warning caps; damage-mask textures use the final WriteTextureSetMap argument and remain unpaletted in software packs. Every glTF buffer requires a positive declared byteLength. Source-world stale checks are dependency-scoped; shared validation rejects malformed collections and extension declarations, ordinary empty meshes, non-affine transforms and nonpositive source partitions, using the current node-level representation for point-only models. World comparison includes texture-directory counts, states and variant links on the world row; reconstruction hashes every input with a 4 GiB aggregate limit; glTF version and 16-bit material values are checked. Source workspace and prepared reads verify content digests despite unchanged stamps. Terrain conversion uses bounded projected triangles and wildcard work, with positive overlaps kept separate; animation wildcard expansion shares a name index and aggregate matching budget. Deep sound declarations retain their format ceilings. Terrain region area/squareUnits is null with areaUnavailable when the bounded clipping calculation cannot finish; metadata and coordinate truncation remain available. List queries filter case-insensitively before pagination and retain record identities. Preview state describes the active viewer; unavailable 3D options are null. Invalid workspace tab requests leave presentation preferences unchanged. Missing structural edit targets return stale_record. Preview capture requires the preview lifetime UUID and returns preview/asset identity; window captures are independent. 3D capture preserves aspect ratio. Explicit camera poses are clamped upright before subsequent movement. Isolation/Show all reject animation previews, matching GUI availability; static pickup isolation uses the complete pickup root. Scene selection and camera mutations preserve active GUI pickup drags by returning busy. Accepted application closing cancels retained preview/editor lifetimes before draining MCP; canceled closing preserves them, and MCP-only disable still permits recovery. Concurrent teardown is shared and cannot reopen access during shutdown. MCP shutdown cancels pending jobs and audio retries without owning retained preview lifetimes; canceled animation level refreshes release their loading overlay. Static LOD/horizon/texture-pack and Whole world difficulty refreshes retain the published scene and options until successful replacement; cancellation restores the saved difficulty. Canceled asset/document loading retries the still-current GUI selection outside the operation scope; navigation/disposal/shutdown suppress obsolete recovery. Superseded MCP scene refreshes report context_changed; failed preparation reports preview_unavailable, with no unpublished preview result. Properties opening verifies publication/identity, links request cancellation, and rechecks pending drafts after decoding. Decoder traversal observes cancellation. Inspection freezes one document revision and links request/document cancellation; disposed or revised results are rejected. Reload stages parsing and guards drafts/revisions/navigation before atomic document replacement, retaining the old document/preview on staging failure. Root/file navigation guards asynchronous publication, including newer pending file loads. GUI browsing keeps pinned Properties drafts. Saves/modal dialogs exclude MCP mutations; read-only state remains available. Approved preview setting drafts apply as one frozen batch and preserve newer input. Late pickup sessions and export/validation reports cannot publish after document closure. Animation binds and late renderer refreshes recover only for originating MCP cancellation; same-editor GUI seek supersession reports context_changed. LOD waits cancel before mutation; pending picker choices cannot leak into another seek. Initial binding and Map/Horizon refreshes reconcile the latest presentation choices and retain playback or explicit Pause. Static refresh ownership survives reentrant status callbacks. Deferred window close preserves new edits/drafts/drag without prompting. Animation v28/v39 open and inspection bound references (4 per table), puffers (4), sequence summaries (16), sequence event previews (8), and raw event/tail bytes (256); counts/truncation flags disclose omissions. Passive JSON omits keyframe streams. Numeric fields and numeric compound callbacks share a 4096-character pre-parse input bound; all vector components validate before mutation, while complete invalid GUI drafts remain intact. animation_records pages bounded event fields; explicit JSON exports remain complete. Model geometry/world lists/sound cues are capped at 32 with counts/truncation; nested metadata uses 512 JSON nodes/8192 text characters (1024 per string, depth 12). Nested polygon/node/material rows and scene lists use 64 nodes/1024 characters per metadata row; scene properties/selection and GUI inspection use the larger budget with inspection_truncated. Superseded mission selections return context_changed; retrying an in-flight choice awaits presentation before persisting settings. Malformed keyframe payloads, including version-39 stored-count mismatches, retain scheduling fields and a read-only diagnostic at segment 0. Preview transforms reject the invalid stream while preserving source bytes. Source projects (roots with data and gamegen folders) open to the map picker, with source_world_list discovery and one map at a time; direct file opening is refused; source_status pages buildable game files with 16 inputs previewed each, and source_export reports built/failed outputs with at most 256 rows, 4 warnings of 128 characters each and 256-character errors (with truncation flags). Source worlds (source_world_open) evaluate GameGen, glTF references, source textures, ZRD resources and animation definitions directly in memory. No preview cache or ZBD archives are created on open, Apply, history or Save. Document path is the mission entry script. sourceWorld reports evaluating, sourceRevision, evaluation diagnostics (64 strings of 512 characters with diagnosticCount/diagnosticsTruncated), workspace revision/history counts, editNotes (16) and lookupChangeCount. Apply validates and accepts source changes in memory; ordinary transforms retain document/viewport resources and structural changes may replace presentation. Commands return the accepted document/revision. Undo/redo is project-wide. save_document atomically writes every dirty owning source through the recoverable project journal; external changes reject publication. Only source_export creates game archives, after pending edits are saved or discarded. Failed or pre-acceptance canceled evaluation leaves the prior scene and history intact; late cancellation cannot retract an accepted edit. Other mutations return busy during evaluation or GUI save. validate evaluates on-disk project sources without accepting pending edits; standard asset export uses the accepted scene's frozen PNG textures. Placement edits change only coordinate tokens of the text resources; object edits change the glTF node or the script instruction that set the value (refused when it ran more than once or uses a macro; a value a script another mission also runs set is set again before this mission's world is written). Copy, delete and re-parent apply to the whole object (a loaded model's root): database glTF nodes are copied, removed or moved in the file; script objects are loaded again before the world is written, commented out, or attached anew. Edits planned from a world whose build inputs changed in the workspace since are refused (stale_document) until it is reloaded. source_changes diffs a working file against the disk off the UI thread (1000 edit lines among at most 200,000 compared lines, up to 2000 shown rows). Escaped diff presentation is charged before decoding rows, at most 1 MiB after reserving workspace details within a 2 MiB service-data allowance. Truncated reports omitted rows; ChangedLines remains the full count or -1 if comparison is bounded. TextTruncated reports line text shortened to 400 characters plus an ellipsis; diff.File and internal source identities remain complete. A concurrent edit, undo, save or project replacement returns context_changed instead of mixing diff content and workspace revisions. Terrain recipes (source_terrain, source_terrain_edit, source_terrain_create, source_terrain_convert) compile to pieces when the mission database is imported: pieces are build outputs, so object edits of them are refused and their recipe is edited instead (recipe edits read the current recipe, so they are not refused in worlds built before another edit). Source-project Blender checkout and update use the bundled RECOIL extension, complete source graphs, stable provenance and one shared undoable transaction. source_blender_extension supplies installation information. Completed exports are hash-verified and placement profiles in other owners remapped before acceptance. Explicit source/texture conflict consent cannot override invalid metadata. Only current version-two graph checkouts are listed; explicitly requested unsupported checkouts require a fresh checkout. Reconstructed source models use physical original-file identities and relative glTF references, with node and polygon attributes embedded in glTF; projects in the external meta/zones.json format are refused, without migration: reconstruct them from the original ZBD files. A placed addition must be the node its AddChild attaches (build_failed otherwise). Changing maps requires saving or explicitly discarding unsaved edits; cancel retains the map. Stale detection compares the build's inputs and the workspace's later changes off the UI thread.
fileOperationResults: Save path previews are bounded before retained result serialization: save_document returns at most 64 written paths of 512 characters each, with writtenCount and writtenTruncated, and saves every file. Other command results preview file paths with the same bounds and Truncated flags. Global state pages complete document identities with offset/limit (maximum 64), total/nextOffset and a 1 MiB escaped metadata allowance before row construction; status text is a 512-character preview with statusTruncated. Source document workspace summaries return counts and undo/redo state; source_changes returns the shared bounded details. Full internal identities are preserved.

interactions.note: The source map's Perspective chip menu items share named views, projection and framing with camera. Follow uses animation_options.followCamera. Projection check states read the live camera.

Numpad views/orbit/pan/zoom/projection/framing and Home use shared semantic operations (in Animation mode and a compiled animation Home and End in the view go to the playback range's start and end: animation_transport seek). Keyboard zoom uses the pointer inside the viewport, otherwise its center, matching camera zoom screenPoint. Native text, Timing and menu keys remain native; Numpad 0 shares Follow camera.

Middle orbit picks a visible scene surface once using rotate screenPoint [x,y] in viewport DIP; empty space retains the pivot. Shift-middle screen pan and Ctrl-Shift-middle dolly use camera pan/dolly. GUI modifier press/release changes the active drag mode regardless of input order, rebasing motion and clearing prior inertia; orbit picking waits for first movement. Wheel/Ctrl-middle zoom refreshes speed from the current pointed surface while moving along the pointer ray; orthographic zoom scales about that point; camera zoom screenPoint matches this, defaulting to viewport center. Misses retain the last speed; pan/orbit do not reset it. Inertia retains the final screen point and resamples from the current camera. Camera reads expose projection, exact axis state, OrbitPivot and NavigationReferenceDistance; automation never captures physical input. Camera-dependent horizons and animation effects refresh after inertial motion at the frame boundary. Floating-card input is excluded from camera wheel handling and gesture starts; native scrolling is presentation-only and complete contents remain available through scene_inspect/scene_card.
View-cube faces use camera view; edges/corners use perspective camera set. The cube uses +Y up and -Z front, matching keyboard/menu axis views.

Archive members list in Assets with stable member UUIDs; the active preview follows the selected member even when Assets is hidden. Aliased payload ranges share immutable decoding. Malformed embedded ZRD remains raw with a warning. Compiled archives are read only: their source project is edited instead.

The typed Data tree uses ordered node UUIDs; standalone ZRD requires complete bounded decoding before its tree is shown. Selection keeps Properties pinned. GUI labels and zrd_nodes bound string prefixes before JSON escaping; MCP marks valueTruncated at 4096 characters. Paging retains only the returned page; ZRD filtering runs off-thread with cancellation/revision checks. Compiled resources are read only.

Virtualized instruction rows share stable script/instruction identities. Read-only reconstructed Text and original Bytes remain separate. Malformed records retain scoped errors and leave valid scripts inspectable/exportable at their authored indices. Selection never executes commands or retargets Properties. Compiled scripts are read only.

AI marker picking and its dynamic Properties context action share snapshot identities with AI discovery and selection. Nodes/arrows use a fixed attack-strategy palette shared with the compiled toolbar's AI nodes tooltip; the selected marker is white. Network/node/selection/Properties results expose attack_strategy value/status/key/characters/truncated/color, with missing strategies red (#FF6666) and empty/unknown/invalid strategies gray (#A0A0A0). Malformed or duplicate strategy fields retain valid graph geometry and produce diagnostics. A compiled Whole world is read only: its markers select and inspect, never move. Hover/selection labels derive from the same node data. Malformed node value types are diagnosed individually while valid neighbors remain visible; malformed duplicate indices remain ambiguous. MW3 constraint queries search bounded network member/name and kind prefixes plus edge/attribute/endpoint labels before pagination, retaining source identities and matching totals. KindCharacters/KindTruncated and ParametersTruncated disclose bounded result previews (kind 256 characters; parameters 64 nodes, depth 8, 2048 text characters, 512 per string). Node/network queries cap authored name/type prefixes before filtering and skip search formatting for empty queries. MW3 links share a 32-slot preview across overlay, cards, Properties and MCP with full counts/truncation; source ZRD paging/export retains all slots. Network diagnostics preview 8 messages at 128 characters, with totals/truncation. Structured strategy values cap 1024 characters. Frame selected uses camera; normal scene framing excludes the overlay.

Shared triangle/instance picking supplies independent hover and selection in the fixed top-right panel. Parent(s) describes the selected object/source-tree occurrence; Surface node and Surface parent(s) identify a clicked internal mesh separately, with glTF indices distinct from compiled slots. Zone (Inherit (ID) when inherited), Altitude zone check and Zone source describe the selected object's zone and what supplied it; Surface zone and Polygon zones describe the clicked mesh and polygon. AI marker cards display read-only Attack strategy among the scrolling details below This AI network node, immediately above Status, and include it once in field copy and scene_card copy-all results; scene_inspect returns structured attackStrategy/hoverAttackStrategy metadata including stored value and network color. The permanent hover readout clears to placeholders over empty space; scene_card select expands details below it and clear collapses details only. Explicit point queries do not move or capture the physical pointer.

The bottom grip and Up/Down/Home/End set the shared inspectionPanelHeight preference without accepting drafts. Total expanded height defaults to 432 DIP, has a normal minimum of 216 DIP and a maximum of 80% of the viewport. Short viewports lower the effective minimum; automatic clamping never overwrites the saved preference. scene_inspect.panel returns preferred/effective heights, current limits and expanded state. Reset layout restores the default; collapsed details retain the preferred expanded height. Explicit height/reset requests supersede active resizing so stale drag updates or cancellation cannot overwrite the newer preference. A docked source-map Properties pane fills its column; the height applies to the top-right card of other previews.

Compiled Whole world cards and selection bounds are read only: they inspect and never edit (scene_card begin refuses them as read_only). Header Isolate and Close and footer Revert/Apply share scene_card revisions, draft lifetimes, history and verified saves. AuthoredPosition, AuthoredRotation and AuthoredHeading bindings enable persistent fields in place. Editable placement fields take input at once (a change starts the draft); Move/Rotate toggles in the Details header show or hide world-axis handles (showing them starts a draft; transformMode move/rotate/none), sharing the draft with scene_card set position/rotationDegrees/headingDegrees. Revert and Apply are enabled only once the draft changes something. Pickups support XYZ radians displayed as degrees; vehicles support native Y heading degrees; Rotate stays hidden for placements without authored rotation. Drags preview until Apply (or Enter in a placement field) creates one combined undo step; Revert (or Escape in a field) discards the draft; Escape during a drag restores that gesture only. Invalid inputs retain the last valid preview and hide handles. Per-field copy (and scene_card copy without a field, MCP only) returns accepted values with labels. World-origin readouts, animation poses and ambiguous actor ownership remain read-only. Header spacing, scrolling and gutter do not change camera or document state. Short viewports automatically place the navigation cube beside the panel, restoring its normal corner when space permits or details close; axis commands remain shared and no physical input is captured. Source-world object fields are editable at once; the Transform header's toggles show Move arrows along the object's own axes or Rotate rings about world X, Y and Z, writing the local Position/Rotation fields (scene_card set fields/transformMode, none hides them); Apply accepts one source transaction and Revert restores the accepted values. Isolate (scene_selection isolate/show_all) shows only the selected object in model and Whole world previews, and again everything when pressed while isolated. In a source map the card is always docked as the Properties pane, without Isolate (the World tree's eyes isolate), and, with nothing selected, Recently selected (scene_inspect recentSelections, then scene_tree select); its footer has icon buttons with immediate tooltips: Copy… and Delete (source_world_object_edit) left of Revert and Apply (scene_card cancel/apply).

A source map's Pickups section always holds Weapons, Ammo and Other (scene_tree category pickupGroup, sectionRow group/count/shown; hide/show/frame, never select), with a row per catalog type inside each under Group by type (scene_options pickupsByType; category pickupType). Pickup rows read as the manual-based short name and a per-type number (Label ERFPG #1); a weapon pickup shows the weapon's render, ammo, health and technology their HUD icons. scene_tree exposes pickupType, pickupKind, pickupGroup, pickupNumber, pickupShortName, pickupName (manual name), instanceName (null on other-difficulty rows) and pickupTemplate from the same catalog classification, and null for non-pickup rows; search matches every word in names, kinds and catalog/game names. Lazy hierarchy rows, bound expansion/selection and viewport reveal share context-scoped occurrence identities, source provenance and pending-draft guards. Source rows expose sourceFile/gltfNode/sourceOccurrence and optional compiledNode. Authored groups removed by compilation remain read-only sourceGroup rows with null node and selectionOwner; whole-reference owners retain framing; their parts appear as exact selectable World child rows, including initialized hidden states. scene_tree hide/show shares source_map_parts_visibility preview overrides; visibility reports the default, own override and effective state. Map picking retains the whole selectionOwner. Preview hierarchy is stable during animation; stored nodes are the fallback. Motion previews scope tree/enumeration/selection/Properties/node framing to the selected assembly and retain original library indices. Expand/collapse/reveal only change presentation. MW3 mission labels use 128-character prefixes with actor NameCharacters/NameTruncated and node metadata name_characters/name_truncated, also available in scene_nodes, scene_properties and pinned Properties. Cards disclose shortened labels; original AIV names and instance identities remain intact. In a source map the World tree adds section rows (scene_tree sectionRow): Zones, AI Networks and Animations list the map's zones, AI networks and .zad definitions (Animations: the map's files directly, then Common, then Objects placed by animations; a definition row's start glyph, grey target text, ⧉, ×N, the opened definition's pressed Open, the kept dot and the amber bar of an animation bound to the selected object are its sectionRow start, target, duplicateOf, bindings, opened, kept and affectsSelection; a binding row leads with its name; the definition rows' AutomationProperties name says how it starts and what it acts on; with Group by start one row per start kind, category definitionGroup); zones and networks are shown one by one with their eyes (all hidden at first), the Zones, AI Networks, AI Vehicles and Pickups rows' master eyes show or hide everything below them, and selecting one opens its card in the docked Properties pane (zone label: source_zone_label; network header: source_ai_network; definitions edit existing events, activation and prerequisites through source_animation and show motion paths through animation_paths). preview_state sections reports the eyes, emphasis, outlines and selection; drafts/resolve_drafts target section covers the card's pending input. Keyboard: Up/Down, Home/End and Page Up/Down move through every shown row (a selectable row becomes the selection; section, folder, file, pass and note rows only take focus), Left/Right reach the row's buttons, Space or Enter opens or closes a row with children or presses the focused button, Escape returns from a button to its row.

Dynamic assembly and LOD pickers, transport, seeker and frame button share the motion sampler and visible viewport. Binding indexes member-scoped ordinal node names once off the UI thread, with cancellation throughout indexing and track binding; superseded results cannot publish. The preview keeps the motion member's UUID; a failed or canceled assembly selection keeps the previous assembly. Overlapping assembly loads retain pre-load playback intent, while explicit Play/Pause during loading takes precedence, including cancellation recovery. State exposes actual playing, loading and playbackRequested. Motion diagnostic previews cap 32 messages at 512 characters with diagnosticCount/diagnosticsTruncated; GUI support text discloses shortened output. Assembly previews cap 32 rows with assemblyCount/assembliesTruncated; motion_preview action assemblies pages all bindings with name filtering. No physical mouse capture.

Authored node conditions and uniquely resolved edge assignments can be outlined, highlighted and framed; node cards navigate to source occurrences in Properties. Runtime valve evaluation is not simulated.

Export ZBD files is a mission × file grid of the plan: All files, Shared files and its six file boxes, a box per section (Map files, rtexture, texture), per column and per mission, All missions, and a cell per file ("–" where the profile builds none), all created from the plan. source_export_selection reads and changes the same globally remembered choices: outputs carry group, kind and section; groups and kinds summarise the header boxes; select/clear take outputs, or groups and kinds (intersecting), or neither for every file; allSelected is the All files box. Build profile is source_profile (source_status lists the profiles), Texture dithering source_dithering, both the Export menu's shared settings, applied at once. Destination is source_export_selection action destination (one folder for every project; destination, destinationExists, destinationExisting and destinationProblem are the field's note). Try again and Read again are get. Closing the window remembers choices and destination even without export. Export is source_export: no outputs when allSelected, else the checked outputs, with the window's destination.

Export > Build profile lists the project's build profiles (source_status profiles: built-in original and modern plus gamegen/build-profiles/*.json, the default marked; a file that cannot be used is shown disabled with its reason, source_status profiles error); the checked one is passed as source_export profile by Export ZBD files and Check source project; the Export ZBD files window's Build profile field shows and changes the same choice. source_profile changes this shared checked selection; omitting profile restores the default, and invalid choices leave it unchanged.

Source-world object editing lives in the selected-object card: a source map always docks it as the Properties pane. The title is the object's name with its class and node number as read-only text (the model in its tooltip); Name and model (where they can change), local Position/Rotation/Scale, supported flags and class-specific commands share an explicit draft. Fields are editable at once: the first change opens the draft, the footer's Apply and Revert end it; focus and Enter do not commit. scene_card set also takes transformMode (move, rotate, none). scene_card set accepts up to 32 fields (field/value strings, 4096 characters each); scene_inspect and drafts target=scene expose the same fields and token. Apply/resolve_drafts accepts one source transaction and undo step, then updates the evaluated scene in memory; input it cannot accept is refused as invalid_draft, shown on the card with the draft kept. Copy/Delete resolve pending input first. scene_properties open focuses this panel; the source tree has no Properties menu. Terrain recipes retain Edit terrain and their dedicated editor. Source ownership, script provenance, rename protections and exclusive crater modes remain enforced. The Zone section's combo box (field zone: inherit, any or 0–254; a load root cannot inherit) and Altitude zone check (field altitudeZoneCheck) join the same draft and write where the occurrence keeps its zone (node, placement override or load root); a shared assignment asks in the GUI and needs scene_card apply sharedScope true over MCP (shared_scope otherwise). Under an unchanged inherited zone the field's hint reads Zone N · inherited from its supplier, with the full source (scene_inspect's Zone source) in its tooltip. The Zone section also shows the read-only Polygon zones of a placed object, group or geometry (one row per zone set with the count of all its polygons, scene_inspect Object polygon zones rows; right-click Copy polygon zones copies them as text); apart from the node number under the title, compiled-node metadata and competing world-origin coordinates are absent from the source-object GUI. The drag-to-scrub axis letters and the Model browse button only fill the same draft fields as scene_card set.

Selecting a zone, AI network or animation definition in the World tree docks its card as the Properties pane (scene_tree select; properties also focuses its first field; Alt+Enter and F2 focus it). A zone's label and a network's header fields are one draft (drafts/resolve_drafts target section) with inline validation: Enter or Apply accepts one undoable change (source_zone_label; source_ai_network edit with the changed keys), Revert or Escape discards it, and selecting elsewhere, saving or closing asks first. A network's card names its fields as the developers' Net Edit dialog does (Attack Radius, Pursuit Radius Min and Max, Buddies Attack…) and says what each does in play, following the chosen type and strategy; source_ai_network read returns each field's label and stored values, and the section draft (drafts target section) reports each row's label, help line, hint, inactive and warning. Store it (shown while Buddies Attack is on in the file without Buddies Activate, which the game then ignores) checks Buddies Activate in the draft; MCP stores it with source_ai_network activate_buddy 1. Paint with this zone engages Edit zones with that zone (source_zone_tool engage). A definition's card in the map layout is read-mostly (source_animation card reads it): Open in Animation mode (the accent button) is animation_mode open with that definition and the card's binding (entry); Bindings' object links select the bound objects (scene_tree select on their rows, which preview_state sections.outlines reports) and their Frame is scene_tree frame on the definition row; Activation, Calls and callers (animation_graph callers) and Source (source_animation context) are read only; Paths are Animation mode's Paths chip and drop windows its Inspector (Definition → Drop windows); the map card has neither. It has no footer: fields are edited in Animation mode's Inspector (SourceSectionCard:Inspector). Close (Esc) clears the selection.

Animation mode's Inspector card (its controls are created in code) is animation_graph inspector (and the inspector of animation_graph select; source_animation card returns the same): kind definition, activation, sequence, event, condition, call or reference, with the header (also shown above the Inspector | Scenario tabs; its Frame is camera framing of the outlined objects and its ✕ is animation_graph select with no node), notices and sections. Field items are source fields of one draft: their boxes, combos, X/Y/Z boxes, Use check boxes, Waits for release and the prerequisite lists are source_animation set changes (by field ID; select and set work in Animation mode only); the Start threshold's clock segments, value, −/+ and ruler are source_animation set startClock/startSeconds (Add threshold sets one, Clear sends the START_TIME field without values); the footer's Revert and Apply are source_animation cancel and apply (one undo step; drafts/resolve_drafts target section), and while a draft is open Play is disabled and the run is stale. Bindings' choice is animation_mode binding and its Frame camera framing of that binding's root; a Condition card's Game/True/False per call path is animation_scenario conditions with that instancePath, its game rule in words (with the current inputs) is the Preview section's info text, Player… is animation_mode layout rightTab scenario; Outcomes rows (animation_runtime conditions) and Occurrences rows (animation_timing marks) seek with animation_transport seek; a call's or a reference node's Included in preview is animation_scenario include with its paths; links select graph nodes and rows (animation_graph select), open and expand reference nodes (animation_mode open, animation_graph expand); the Run sections read animation_runtime sequences/instances. Notices sections are animation_runtime notices for the item: a card lists the notices that name its item expanded (refused or ignored starts, unavailable calls, excluded calls that would change the run, limits, notes about it; an excludedEffect's Include, an actions item with action includePath (its call path), is animation_scenario include with that notice's excludedEffect.includePaths and included true); the preview's generic approximations are one collapsed line on the definition's card ("4 preview approximations ▸", an item of type noticeGroup; animation_runtime notices marks them generic). Drop windows (only for a definition with recognised flight-to-callback-911 calls) is animation_paths without a definition: Analyze drop windows is show (analyze with an entry), the admitted callsites and "Drop analysis follows the scenario's condition switches" are preview_state.parachute callsites and policy, the window list (window, flight sequence start, duration) is its windows, a click selects (select), Move along path and the start box begin a draft (begin; set with start or segment and fraction), Apply / Revert are confirm / cancel (one undo step). The view's paths are the Paths chip (MainWindow.AnimationPaths:PathsChip).

Animation definition sequence/event selection and typed fields share source_animation read/begin/set/apply/cancel with revision and draft token guards. Selection and expansion inspect structure without player construction, duration measurement, audio or path evaluation. Every object card (the player tank's too) ends with Animations affecting this object: the first 8, then Show n more lists the rest (scene_tree animationUses on the object's row pages every one; the row's animationUses holds the first 8 and animationUseCount the total): each row selects its definition in the World tree (scene_tree select) and its Open enters Animation mode (animation_mode open with that definition and entry); names are literal text. In Animation mode an object picked in the view adds Events naming it in the opened definition (each selects its row: animation_graph select); scene_inspect animations reports both sections (affecting, eventsNaming). Paths belong to Animation mode's Paths chip (MainWindow.AnimationPaths:PathsChip), for the binding it plays (animation_mode binding): Show guides only toggles compatible cached paths; animation_paths analyze evaluates explicitly, frame frames cached paths, clear releases the cache. Analysis is independent of the main frame, audio, camera and panel view. Kind is object or camera (teal/orange). Source preview and paths use initialized standable terrain; procedural object motion stops at world Y -500/500 without impact cues, while keyframes/cameras remain unrestricted. The Drop windows section of a flight's Definition card (Animation mode) uses animation_paths without definition and its own snapshot/purpose; its callback conditions follow the map's animation scenario (player, condition switches, rules), a change to them marks the shown analysis stale until show runs again, and on a compiled Whole world animation_scenario inputs {player} sets that player (animation_options activationTarget is refused as moved); its certified move changes the CALL offset while preserving the paired STOP duration. Generic event editing remains available and invalidates the prior window analysis.

Animation mode's Paths chip over the 3D view (created in code): its state word (not evaluated, evaluating, shown, hidden, out of date, partial) and status line are animation_paths state's chip. Evaluate paths is analyze with the opened definition (its binding, the scenario and its included paths; silent: the playhead, camera and panel stay), Show guides show/hide, Frame paths frame, Clear cached paths clear (all with definition); Show range tests and Contacts and impacts are overlay with rangeTests and contacts; the contacts (⊥) and impact sounds (◎) it marks are markers. Progress and failures go to the chip and the transport's status line, never to Diagnostics opening.

The 3D view's range rings (drawn in code, no input): a selected or hovered PLAYER_RANGE question or range-gated activation draws its ring around the attach node, the player pin and the dashed line labelled with the distance and outcome (an edge arrow with the distance when the player is off screen); animation_graph select returns its rangeDrawing, animation_paths ranges lists every range test of the opened animation and its expanded calls (drawn: whether the view draws it now) and animation_runtime player the player reference (position, source, frozen) at the playhead. Guides carry a dot at the playhead and faint ticks every second; a selected motion event emphasises its guide (alpha only).

Timing's Drop windows lane (drawn in code) under the opened flight's sequence lane: each analyzed window on every flight cycle the run reached, as a bar on the flight sequence's clock. A click selects the window (animation_paths select); a drag (past 3 DIP; 0.025 s grid, Shift 0.1 s, Ctrl free) moves its start only (begin, then set start), and Apply / Revert in the Inspector are confirm / cancel.

While Move along path moves a window in the view, the banner "Moving drop window 2 · click a point on the flight path · right-click or Esc cancels" shows (preview_state.parachute moving and draft.pointer): a click places the start (set with segment and fraction) and keeps the draft for Apply; Cancel, a right-click or Esc reverts (cancel). It ends with Exit, the map and a rebuild.

Animation mode's Timing view (the run on the shared clock, in seconds) is animation_timing with the GUI's identities. Its rows are animation_timing lanes: the Starts lane (one ▼ per scenario start; a caution dot where the scenario's prerequisite rule let an unmet start run; refused starts in the rose colour), instance groups (the binding, started, its binding-state band; called instances nested under their caller, grouped by definition as the graph groups them) and sequence lanes (state glyph). Marks and state bands are animation_timing marks for a lane (executed, interval (a stop cut short ends at the stop, with a cap, and carries stopped), running, condition with T/F and forced, skipped, excluded, duplicate, blocked, release with targetLane, loop, refused, unresolved; bands waitingRelease, waitingThreshold, paused, blocked, stopped, complete, binding); a count badge clusters marks within 4 DIP and its hover lists them; a group row's dashed marker is an excludedEffect notice (animation_runtime notices) on that lane at its excludedEffect.seconds, with its marker text. A click on a lane label (↑/↓) is animation_timing select (the Inspector, the graph's node and the 3D outlines follow; the Starts lane opens the Scenario tab); a click on a mark (Ctrl+←/→ on the selected lane, or a Log row) is occurrence (select and seek). A group's chevron, a double-click or Enter is expand. Dragging a start (0.025 s; Shift 0.1 s; Ctrl free), its UI Automation value, and right-click → Remove start are animation_scenario starts; starts at one time are one marker with a count, whose click list only chooses which of them a drag moves (presentation; each start keeps its own slider and Remove). The ruler's click or drag, ←/→ (one 1/60 s tick; Shift 1 s) and Home/End are animation_transport seek; its "+5 s" at the playback range's end is animation_transport extend. The view bar's Lanes | Log, Thresholds, Fit range ▾ (range, run, selection), Ctrl+wheel and Shift+wheel on the clock and the label grip are animation_timing options (view, thresholds, fit, visibleRange, labelWidth). With Thresholds on and an event selected, its bracket end's drag is animation_timing threshold (the same source_animation draft; apply or cancel there). The Log's Copy and Follow latest are presentation; log pages its rows with retained and discarded counts. F2 focuses the Inspector's start threshold (source_animation).

The Inspector's start threshold, in seconds only: the seconds box, −/+ 0.025 s (Shift 0.1 s) and the ruler's diamond (0.025 s grid; Shift 0.1 s; Ctrl free) update the same source_animation draft (set with the event's START_TIME field, or startClock and startSeconds with the event's record) as Timing's bracket drag and animation_timing threshold. Viewing preserves negative and off-grid thresholds exactly. Apply is one history transaction; Save and Export remain separate. Verified drop-window move grips use animation_paths set/confirm and never resize the paired STOP duration.

Animation mode's panel. The view bar's Structure tools are listed under AnimationGraphView:Controls and Timing's under AnimationTimingView:Controls. The transport row: Play/Pause (Space), Stop, Go to range start, step back and forward one 1/60 s tick (, and .) are animation_transport play/pause/stop/start/previous/next; the time box seeks in seconds (animation_transport seek); the range button (of 0–X s) and its flyout read animation_transport's rangeState (Auto or Custom, why Auto ends there: text and auto, measuring), the flyout's start and end are animation_options playbackRange (Custom), its Extend +5 s is animation_transport extend, Auto is animation_transport auto (it measures again when needed) and Fit range to starts is animation_scenario fitRange (each asks about a pending draft first; Auto is measured in the background as the definition opens and again after a scenario change, never playing; until it arrives the range shows no end, of 0–… s, and rangeState.measuring is true); Speed, Loop range, Mute, Volume and Follow camera are animation_options speed/replay/mute/volume/followCamera (in ⋯ below 1,040 DIP; the toggles apply from their checked state, so a UI Automation Toggle is a click; all five also apply with a source draft open). The status line is animation_transport's state (Evaluated 0–t s · n occurrences, Stale, Not evaluated), the run's latest status message (path progress, audio), the hint while the playhead rests at an end the 5 s rule set while the run goes on (rangeState.hint: "Ended 5 s after the last timed event · motion may continue", or "Ended at the last sound or effect tail · …" when a tail outlasts the 5 s, "Ended where every spin has gone round once · …" when a constant spin's first revolution does), whose Extend +5 s is animation_transport extend with play true (it lengthens the range and plays on; the flyout's and the ruler's only lengthen it), or the last preview failure (trimmed at its end, the whole text in its tooltip), whose Show in Diagnostics is animation_mode layout diagnostics. The view bar's ⚠ n chip lists the opened animation's notices (animation_runtime notices; each Go to is animation_graph select of its node or row, or animation_timing select of its lane; an excludedEffect's Include, created in code, is animation_scenario include with its excludedEffect.includePaths and included true; its checking state (n · checking…) is the excludedCheck notice's excludedCheck.checking; Show in Diagnostics is animation_mode layout diagnostics), and the same counts are the ⚠ badges on graph nodes and Timing lanes (each notice's node and lane; an excludedEffect also counts on its excludingCall.referenceNode and affected.node). The legend ⓘ (edges, Timing marks, states, families) is help topic animation-mode. The view bar's Structure | Timing | Split (Ctrl+1/2/3; Split needs 1,300 DIP) is animation_mode layout view; its splitter keeps the session's share; the view tools a narrow panel has no room for are under ⋯ (More view tools), the same controls with the same tools; each ⋯ flyout opens with its first control focused, Tab cycles inside it and Esc returns to ⋯ (presentation only). The first-entry tip's dismissal is remembered for the profile (presentation only).

Animation mode's Structure view (the panel's default view; Split at 2,560 DIP): the opened binding's node graph is animation_graph read (nodes, edges with their routed points, a sequence's rows and blocks, each with its run at the playhead: a row's now, ✓ and stopped are its run disposition current, executed and stopped), with the GUI's identities. A click on a header, row, question, branch label or closing line, or ↑/↓ through them, is animation_graph select (the Inspector card, the 3D outlines of the nodes it names, Timing's lane scrolled into view with its group opened; Esc or a click on empty space selects nothing); a click on an edge selects its source row; → follows a row's edge and ← goes back to its source. A sequence's chevron, a header double-click, Enter and ←/→ on a header are expand/collapse with node; Show all n events is expand with showAll; a grouped row's chevron is expand/collapse with row; Collapse all and Expand all are collapse/expand with all. A reference node's Expand ▸ (double-click, Enter) is expand/collapse with node (one frame per group, at most 64 expanded) and its Open ▷ (Ctrl+Enter) animation_mode open on its definition and first binding; the expanded frame header's member switcher is expand with node and member (read reports the frame's group, members and memberIndex). A blocked sequence's Blocked › link is select with its run's blockedBy edge (the waiting call row), then the port is the include toggle. The Game · True · False switch on every IF and ELSEIF outcome line (G, T, F on a selected question) is animation_scenario conditions with the frame's call path ("" for the opened binding), and a pip of its outcome line or pass strip seeks to its pass (animation_transport seek; read rows report where the pips are drawn). A call row's port is its include toggle: animation_scenario include with the edge's paths (included excludes them, else includes them); its ⚠ and tooltip for an excluded call that would change the run are the excludedEffect notices whose excludingCall.edge is that edge (animation_runtime notices). Include ▾ is animation_scenario includeAll (All calls), includeAll with scope opened (This animation only: every path below the opened binding's start, the other starts' calls excluded with their marked ones) or excludeAll (None). Fit (Ctrl+0), the zoom menu, − and + (Ctrl+= / Ctrl+−), Ctrl+wheel at the pointer, wheel and Shift+wheel scrolling, middle-drag, a drag on empty space, Space+drag, and the minimap are animation_graph viewport (zoom, center, fit, reveal); Run overlay is viewport runOverlay; Re-run to here on a stale overlay is animation_transport seek to the last run's time. F2 on a selected row focuses the Inspector's start threshold (source_animation). Tooltips are presentation only.

The Scenario tab shows animation_scenario read and changes it with the same actions: a start's seconds and ✕ and + Add start… (a searchable list of every binding) are starts; Fit range to starts is fitRange; Include all / Exclude all are includeAll / excludeAll; a group's or a path's box is include (paths, included); Player At start / No player are inputs player, Custom and Pick in view are pick (target player; the view's next click; MCP gives screenPoint); Random seed, Effects detail, Phase, Height and the beam origin's clear are inputs; the beam origin's Pick in view is pick (target beamOrigin); an override's ✕ is conditions with value game and Go to selects its event (animation_graph select); the rules' segments are rules; the caution card at the top (what a source edit left unmatched, kept and marked) is read's unmatched, and its Remove and Keep are unmatched with resolve remove or keep and the kind (starts, paths, conditions), with a draft open too (the kept kinds are saved with the scenario); Reset… then Reset is reset. Any change, from either, shows at once in the tab, the chip and the run.

Animation mode's command bar and status bar: Exit animation is animation_mode exit; the definition picker (searchable) is animation_mode open with the definition, the binding picker animation_mode binding, ‹ › animation_mode back/forward; the scenario chip shows animation_scenario read's summary and opens the Scenario tab (animation_mode layout rightTab scenario). The status bar's "Animation mode · name" is animation_mode state; after Exit its "Animation scenario kept · n starts" re-enters on the kept definition (animation_mode open; state keptScenario). The Animation menu's items in a map are animation_mode open (with the selected definition) and open with keptScenario's definition, and in the mode animation_transport play/pause/stop/previous/next, animation_mode layout rightTab scenario and exit. The World tree and Diagnostics toggles in the mode are animation_mode layout tree/diagnostics (workspace_view navigator/tools in the mode change the same two); the panel's splitter is layout panelHeight, and the splitter of the Diagnostics strip under the panel (created in code) is layout panelHeight and diagnosticsHeight (given at most the room the panel leaves, at least 96, and reported as shown; workspace_view toolsHeight in the mode sets the same height; the map layout's Diagnostics keeps its own).

Shift+Esc is animation_mode exit (plain Esc never exits); Alt+←/→ are back/forward; Ctrl+1/2/3 are layout view structure/timing/split; Space is animation_transport play or pause outside text fields and focused buttons; , and . are previous/next (one 1/60 s tick), with Shift a seek of one second; Home and End in the 3D view are animation_transport seek to the playback range's start and end. F6 / Shift+F6 (focus: 3D view, transport, panel, Inspector) and Alt+Enter (the Inspector's first field) only move the keyboard focus; Esc, after what is in progress, clears the selection (animation_graph select with no node). A compiled animation takes the same keys apart from Alt+←/→ and Shift+Esc (CompiledAnimationKey; animation_mode layout and animation_transport on its preview): Esc ends its Pick in view, then clears its selection (animation_graph select with no node). help topic animation-mode lists every key and pointer action.

Pick in view's banner ("Click a surface to place the player · Esc cancels") takes the next left click on a surface of the 3D view: animation_scenario pick with target and that point (screenPoint, DIP). A right click, Esc or Cancel ends it without a change (the middle button still orbits); Exit and the end of the mode end it too.

Properties of a terrain piece edits its recipe: recipe and surface defaults (attribute inputs; empty removes an override), regions in order (select, move up/down, delete, add, rename, surfaces, attributes, cover whole surfaces), the brush (radius, paint or erase in viewport) and Paint polygon / Erase polygon: typed plan-view corners (x z pairs separated by commas, a semicolon starting each hole, at most 65,536 characters) that map to source_terrain_edit paint with polygons (mode paint or erase), read by the same recipe shape parser with its ring and coordinate refusals; the round brush cannot draw such exact edges, and a larger shape is painted in parts, painting being a union. Properties shows 32 regions per page with native Previous/Next actions. MCP uses source_terrain pagination for the same ordered regions. source_terrain pages recipe lists and region lists with offset/nextOffset (at most 64 rows), retaining exact paths and names. Each edit is source_terrain_edit with the same recipe, region and attribute patch; the brush selection itself is presentation state.

While the brush is on, a left-button drag over a source world collects the surface points under the pointer; on release the stroke's plan-view path and the brush radius paint or erase the brush's region as one undoable change (source_terrain_edit paint with path and radius). Escape or lost capture drops a stroke in progress; MCP never synthesizes pointer input.

The zone picker's text box (0–254, Any or a label; Enter picks), arrow keys and rows choose the zone (source_zone_tool engage with zone; state lists the map's zones with labels and polygon counts as placed in the world). Zones are named in the World tree's zone card (source_zone_label), not in the picker.

While the tool is engaged, a left-button drag paints or erases its zone on each paintable source polygon the pointer crosses (looking through models the tool cannot paint); release applies the stroke as one undoable change: source_polygon_zones with the source polygons source_zones inspection returns. Ctrl held inverts the mode for a stroke, Shift+click picks a zone of the polygon under the pointer and [ ] step through the used zones (source_zone_tool engage with mode or zone), and Esc drops a stroke in progress. MCP never synthesizes pointer input.

After a stroke, notices under the tool banner report the full polygons it skipped, with Show/Hide outlining them (source_zone_tool showSkipped or hideSkipped; state lastStroke lists them), editable terrain it crossed and its polygon limit; ✕ dismisses a notice.

Outside text fields, P and E engage the tool in Paint or Erase (or switch its mode), [ and ] step through the zones the map uses, and Esc leaves the tool once no stroke is in progress (a stroke in progress is dropped first): source_zone_tool engage or exit. Ctrl and Shift only change the cursor and banner until a stroke or click uses them.

The Add model dialog (Tools > Add model to world, shown unavailable for now) lists project models (source_world_models) with a filter (a virtualized list of at most 2000 matches, with a note when the filter matches more), suggests the model's name as node name, offers unplaced or placed (position and heading, defaulting to the orbit pivot), and filters/pages all other missions' definition files for the name (source_world_definitions: query, offset, limit 1–64, nextOffset, filtered total and unfiltered fileCount). Full paths remain usable; large rows shorten MCP pages before projection. Model listing observes workspace cancellation and refuses a project replacement with context_changed. The GUI retains checked files across pages, selecting at most 64. Lists up to 64 start checked; larger lists start unchecked (source_world_add_model refuses to add such a list whole); Add maps to source_world_add_model with complete checked paths from any pages, including long project paths. Completion definitionFiles previews keep at most 64 paths of 512 characters with definitionFileCount and definitionFilesTruncated; discovery and editing retain full identities.

Tools and the Pickups section context menu open the same dialog. Catalog type, explicit position, Euler degrees, amount, respawn and difficulty use the shared source append transaction; template spawning is verified before acceptance. Pending drafts and stale revisions refuse creation.

Source-project Blender checkout and update use the bundled RECOIL extension, complete source graphs, stable provenance and one shared undoable transaction. source_blender_extension supplies installation information. Completed exports are hash-verified and placement profiles in other owners remapped before acceptance. Explicit source/texture conflict consent cannot override invalid metadata. Only current version-two graph checkouts are listed; explicitly requested unsupported checkouts require a fresh checkout.

Export ZBD files and Check source project run source_export inside a modal progress window that blocks the workspace below: the game file being built and how many of how many, then the lookup check and writing. Its Cancel, Escape or closing it cancels the run, as zstudio_operation cancel does for an MCP job; MCP runs show no window and poll the operation.

GUI Initialize and source_reconstruct share reconstruction placement: m6 lasdesig goes to data/common/models; m4 train, rcar1, trnsplsh and their referenced tturret go to data/m4/models when provenance and safe lookup agree. Existing projects are not migrated. The Initialize source project dialog's retail ZBD folder and source project folder (typed or browsed) are source_reconstruct's source and destination; Initialize and open (enabled once both are given) runs it with open true, showing its progress and refusals in the dialog, and Cancel or closing the dialog cancels the running operation (zstudio_operation cancel), which removes what it wrote; a Cancel that comes once the project is written leaves it unopened in its folder, as a cancel before source_reconstruct has made it the workspace root does (a later cancel changes nothing: a source project is not indexed, so the operation completes with the project open and indexComplete true); a refusal, including a folder it could not remove, stays shown in the dialog.

The window's Browse buttons choose files with the Windows dialog; world_compare takes their full paths instead. Compare maps to world_compare. Tree rows, their expansion and selection (which shows the row's properties in both worlds, read page by page with propertyOffset) map to world_compare_tree read/expand/collapse/select; the Differences only checkbox and the name filter map to its differencesOnly and query arguments, which filter MCP reads without changing the window's controls (windowFilter reports them).

The Create terrain dialog's checked meshes (filtered and paged 64 at a time, at most 256 chosen) are source_terrain_create's surfaces, and its Recipe field (starting at the file's name.terrain.json) is its recipe: another path lets a second mission's terrain use the same surfaces file, or a terrain be created again while an unused recipe keeps the default name. A name not ending in .terrain.json is refused in the dialog; a path outside the data folder or one that exists is refused by the shared creation, as for MCP. Cancel creates nothing.

Enter applies and Escape reverts the active drop-window move (Move along path, the start box or a Timing lane drag); native controls retain their keyboard behavior. Escape also cancels an in-progress flight analysis.

Exact window selection and path movement emit ordered segment/fraction identities. Preview moves all release markers of one window, preserving separate visits at path crossings. No MCP operation captures physical input.

Reads refuse a malformed settings file with invalid_argument; setting the dithering replaces a damaged file.

With every file selected Export passes no outputs, so source_export builds every file and sizes automatic packs from the textures as built; otherwise the exact checked outputs. The Zones group's Edit zones toggle engages the tool (in its last mode and zone) or leaves it: source_zone_tool engage or exit. Engaged, the tool draws its own zone view and the overlays pause with their buttons disabled (scene_options highlight and faceOrientation return busy); leaving resumes them.
The Paint | Erase switch beside the engaged toggle sets the mode: source_zone_tool engage with mode.
The zone dropdown opens the zone picker (ZonePicker:Controls); source_zone_tool state lists the same zones with labels and polygon counts as placed in the world.
The tool banner's Exit leaves the tool, as Esc does: source_zone_tool exit.

Tools > Convert to editable terrain shows the plan (source_terrain_convert without apply), converts after confirmation as one undoable change and reports the altitude probe comparison (source_terrain_convert with apply). Ordinary recipes preserve converted runs in database encounter order. plan.recipe retains the first recipe; plan.recipes gives a bounded total/items/omitted summary. After acceptance, recipeListing identifies the existing read-only source_terrain command and replacement document for complete recipe pages. A bounded comparison reports complete=false and limitation when its work or index budget is exceeded, without failing the accepted conversion; plan reason previews disclose reasonTruncated.
Tools → Compare worlds… opens the one Compare worlds window; world_compare opens the same window and compares two files given by full path.

Numeric transform input and world axis update the shared frozen-selection draft, preserving incomplete input until explicit confirmation or cancellation.

The back arrow left of the Whole world heading (Maps) returns to the source map picker after resolving drafts and save/discard/cancel. MCP closes the current document explicitly, requiring revision and discard consent for unsaved edits. Newer navigation supersedes pending map opening.

A source map's status-bar pane toggles: navigator (World tree), inspector (docked Properties) and tools (Diagnostics: the problems alone, read with zstudio_problems); the World tree and Properties are session-only, while Diagnostics shown/hidden and its height are remembered in the project's .zstudio/settings.json; never the compiled explorer's preferences.
The source map's Perspective chip menu runs the same projection, named view and framing actions as camera view/projection/frame.
The Flycam banner's Exit ends Fly like Escape; agents navigate with camera without capturing the user's physical mouse.
Collapse all is scene_tree collapse on the expanded rows (presentation only).

The outliner search box is scene_tree read with search: a flat list of matches with their parent paths (types optionally narrows it by the legend's categories). The info button's legend is static; rows carry category and pass in scene_tree read.
Choosing a flat match is scene_tree select on its row.

A row's Frame selection is scene_tree select on that row, then camera frame target selected. On the Pickups section's Weapons, Ammo and Other rows and their type rows (never selected) it is scene_tree action frame on that row; on an animation definition or binding row it frames what it binds to without selecting: scene_tree action frame on that row (shown only when sectionRow frameable: a definition bound only to templates has no Frame, and frame refuses it; hidden below a 260 DIP pane).

A definition row's Open (▷), or a binding row's under a definition with several bindings (also on their search results), is animation_mode open with that definition (and the binding's entry); Enter on the row or result and a double-click do the same. A click on the row only selects it and shows its card (scene_tree select). The opened definition's Open is pressed (sectionRow opened).

The Animations row's Group by start toggle is scene_options changes.animationsByStart (preview_state sections.animationsByStart): the map's and Common's definitions in one row per start kind (scene_tree category definitionGroup) instead of by file. For the session; off at first.
The Animations row's context menu item Group by start is the same scene_options changes.animationsByStart as the row's toggle.

A definition or binding row's context menu Select <object> (shown when it binds one object a World tree row lists) is scene_tree select with that object's node (the definition's sectionRow rootNodes, the binding's rootNode).

A row's animated mark opens a flyout of every animation affecting the object (it scrolls, and says "and n more" for what it cannot list): scene_tree animationUses on that row pages them all (the row's animationUses holds the first 8); each one's row selects its definition (scene_tree select) and its Open is animation_mode open with that definition and entry.
A definition or binding row's context menu Open in Animation mode is animation_mode open with that definition (and entry).
Copy animation name copies the row's name; scene_tree read returns it as the row's label (no clipboard side effect is needed).
Animation mode's pane header ✕ clears the selection (as Esc does after everything else): animation_graph select with no node; the Inspector shows the opened definition again.

The pane header's Frame frames what the selection names (animation_graph select reports outlined) or the bound objects: camera frame target selected after the selection, or scene_tree frame on the definition row.

A definition or binding row's context menu Frame bound objects (a binding's: Frame <its object>) is scene_tree action frame on that row; it waits when nothing it binds to is drawn in the view (frame refuses it).
A definition row's context menu Show source opens a flyout with the definition's source excerpt: source_animation context with record settings.
A definition row's context menu Properties (Alt+Enter) is scene_tree properties on that row: it selects it and focuses its card.
Animation mode's right pane tabs Inspector | Scenario are animation_mode layout rightTab inspector or scenario.

A row's eye is scene_tree hide/show (view only, no source edit). Zones and AI networks are shown one by one and start hidden: a zone's eye shows or hides its colour and a network's its nodes and links (any shown zone turns the zone overlay on, any shown network the AI overlay). The Zones, AI Networks, AI Vehicles and Pickups rows' master eye, and those of the Pickups section's Weapons, Ammo and Other rows and their type rows (scene_tree hide/show on that row; rows report master), hides or shows everything below them; it changes when pressed, or when everything below comes to be shown (or hidden) one by one. preview_state sections reports the section and pass masters; group and type rows report theirs as master on their scene_tree rows. scene_selection show_all shows every hidden object (units and pickups too), not zones or networks. In a source map a show (scene_tree show, show_all) also selects in the view an object the card shows as hidden because it was selected in the tree while hidden, when no draft is open, so its placement can be edited; with an ai_path or parachute draft open it follows once that draft ends and the application is idle, after the command returned (read scene_inspect or preview_state afterwards).

Middle-clicking a world object's eye isolates it (scene_tree isolate on the row, which rows report as isolated; for an object, the same as scene_selection isolate with its node); middle-clicking the isolated row's eye shows everything again (scene_tree isolate on that row; rows hidden with the eye stay hidden, unlike scene_selection show_all). Ending or moving an isolation (and scene_selection isolate or show_all) selects in the view an object the card shows as hidden because it was selected in the tree while hidden, as a show does. Zones, AI networks, units and pickups have no isolation in a map (scene_tree isolate refuses them; scene_selection isolate refuses units and pickups as unsupported).

The Zones header's Objects | Polygons switch is scene_options changes.highlight zones or polygonZones: the kind of colour the shown zones take. It is disabled while no zone shows and paused while Edit zones is on (busy).

The Pickups row's Group by type toggle is scene_options changes.pickupsByType (preview_state sections.passes.pickupsByType): inside Weapons, Ammo and Other a row per catalog type (scene_tree category pickupType). For the session; off at first.
The Pickups row's context menu item Group by type is the same scene_options changes.pickupsByType as the row's toggle.

File > Open workspace… (Ctrl+O): open_root with project true, which refuses a folder that is not a source project (not_project, naming the missing data or gamegen folder), one that is or lies below a link, or one in an earlier source format.

Help > Check for updates: update_check action check asks GitHub now (an explicit request, also with automatic checks off); the status bar item shows Checking for updates…, then Update available or the result for a few seconds. A private test profile never contacts GitHub.

Help > Check for updates automatically: update_check action automatic with enabled (saved setting, default on; at most one check a day after zStudio starts). state and update_check report it as update.automatic.

The status bar's Update available item (directly left of Preview notices) opens update.url, a page of github.com/Vorta/zStudio/releases, in the browser; MCP returns the url (state update or update_check) and opens nothing on the user's desktop. Clicking a check's result dismisses it.

animationAssociationResults: scene_tree animations includes initial-root and statically known indirect recipients. animationUses contains the first eight entryIndex/name/origin/reason records; origin is initialRoot or indirect. animationUseCount is how many there are (at most 256 per object) and animationUsesTruncated discloses that more exist; scene_tree action animationUses pages every one, uncapped, as the object card (Show n more) and the glyph flyout list them. animationHasInitialRoot and animationHasIndirect retain both origin summaries when details are capped. GUI tree/search uses #6FC8D6 for any initial root, #89B5BC for indirect-only recipients; same glyph and opacity. Read-only position references and unknown impact targets are excluded.
